svg.title: Horspool's search for woman along line 3284 of the book: compare from the pattern's last byte, and let the byte of the text under it say how far to move on
svg.text: the shift table: how far the byte under the pattern's last byte moves it on

g.title: At 0: "a" under the pattern's last byte is not "n". "a" is in the pattern 1 from its end: move on 1, which puts the pattern's "a" under it.
At 1: the last 2 bytes match, then a space is not "m". "n" is in the pattern only as its last byte: move on 5, the whole length.
At 6: the last 1 bytes match, then "i" is not "a". "n" is in the pattern only as its last byte: move on 5, the whole length.
At 11: "," under the pattern's last byte is not "n". "," is not in the pattern at all: move on 5, the whole length.
At 16: "h" under the pattern's last byte is not "n". "h" is not in the pattern at all: move on 5, the whole length.
At 21: "o" under the pattern's last byte is not "n". "o" is in the pattern 3 from its end: move on 3, which puts the pattern's "o" under it.
At 24: all 5 bytes are the same, compared from the last back to the first: a match. grep backs up to the start of the line and prints it.
The whole search: Horspool tried 7 positions and compared 14 bytes of text, 12 different ones; trying every position, the scan compares 30 to find the same match.
g.text: in the accent: the bytes each one compared; the others it never looked at
